questions.text: How long have you had genital itching, and is it constant or does it come and go?
questions.purpose: Characterise duration and pattern of genital itch to guide differential diagnosis

questions.text: Is there any visible rash, redness, discharge, or sores in the affected area?
questions.purpose: Identify associated dermatological or infective findings that change management

questions.text: Have you had recent sexual contact that may have exposed you to an STI?
questions.purpose: STI exposure with genital itch requires STI screen for pubic lice, trichomoniasis, herpes, or other infections

questions.text: Is the itch worse at night and do close contacts have similar symptoms?
questions.purpose: Nocturnal itch with household spread strongly suggests scabies or pubic lice infestation

questions.text: Have you recently used new soaps, creams, condoms, or laundry products that may have caused irritation?
questions.purpose: Contact or irritant dermatitis is a common cause of genital itch

questions.text: Do you have poorly controlled diabetes or take immunosuppressant medications?
questions.purpose: Diabetes and immunosuppression predispose to candidal or other fungal genital infections causing itch

questions.text: Have you noticed persistent itch without any rash, or any white patches or colour changes on the skin?
questions.purpose: White plaques or persistent itch without rash may suggest lichen sclerosus or dermatosis requiring specialist assessment
